chunk_findings.detail: The retry auto-approve is gated by `if canon.site.min_level <= 1:`. The intent says this feature is for the generic T2 verbs `complete.force`, `claim.force`, `gate.skip.failed_review`, and `approve.partial`, which are T2 asks and therefore require `canon.site.min_level == 2`. With `auto_approve_after_retries=1`, after one prior refusal of `complete.force` for the same digest, `refusals(state, canon)` is `1` and `n >= threshold` would be true, but the outer `<= 1` guard is false, so `auto_answer` returns `None` and the second filing is not auto-approved. The feature is a no-op for all of the verbs it was explicitly meant to handle.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py auto_answer retry gate

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify the rule is count-based rather than window-based, but `_frozen_clock(monkeypatch)` is never advanced between the first and second `C.operator_gate` calls. With both filings at the same frozen time, a window-based implementation using any positive window would still see the second filing inside that window and would also pass this test. It therefore does not fail the bug it is intended to catch.
